required_units: The retained behavior-tree evidence supports at least four unique source-qualified recovery invocations, not exactly four over the goal lifetime.
The ordered retained recovery leaves and terminal states are Spin success, Wait success, BackUp success, and Spin success.
Each retained invocation follows a ComputePathToPose failure, NavigateWithReplanning failure, successful WouldAPlannerRecoveryHelp check, and system-recovery entry.
The NavigateToPose action eventually succeeded, so recovery did not prevent recorded task success.
The maximum Nav2 feedback recovery count of 16 is not treated as 16 unique recovery invocations.
The answer withholds a physical cause, unique obstacle identity, and exact costmap consumption.
The answer recommends time-aligned plans and hash-checked costmaps around a planner failure as a discriminating next check.
prohibited_claims: Exactly four recovery attempts occurred over the complete goal lifetime.
Sixteen unique behavior-tree recovery invocations occurred.
Recovery caused the navigation action to fail.
A named obstacle or physical enclosure caused planning to fail.
The delivered costmap was proven to be the exact planner-consumed state.

limits: The retained count is a lower bound because whole-history completeness is not proven.
Software execution ordering does not identify the physical cause of planner failure.
Delivered costmaps do not prove exact planner consumption.
This episode is development evidence, not held-out or confirmatory evidence.
